description: Lan is Ukrainian for a large farm field. We are a small team from Ukraine working on Field Shift. One of us lives in a farming village and has worked in agriculture, and we bring software development and machine learning skills. Our goal is to turn NASA data into something a real farmer would actually use. We welcome teammates with experience in GIS and remote sensing, agronomy, or UI design.
summary:
Lan is a web app that turns NASA Earth observations into a crop-rotation plan for any field in Ukraine and the 48 contiguous US states. Tap a field on the map and its card shows what grew there in each of the last eleven seasons, what to sow next, what to avoid and until which year, the climate risks for each crop counted as "in x of the last 20 years", and what to watch during the season. A comparison screen lays out three rotations and the farmer's own plan on one calendar, scored on water, heat, soil and disease, with good and bad crop sequences explained.

Crop history comes from NASA HLS greenness (30 m, Landsat + Sentinel-2, 2016-2026) for 597,203 Ukrainian fields; NASA POWER gives 35 years of daily weather per cell. Our winter / summer / bare history agrees with independent Ukrainian crop maps on 95.3 % of held-out field-seasons (79-95 % in five other zones). In the USA (15.97 million fields) the 2018-2025 history is USDA's Cropland Data Layer.

Rotation mistakes are made once and paid for years. Lan gives a farmer a second opinion grounded in their own field's past and their district's changing climate. Every recommendation names its evidence and gaps, and the farmer can correct any season.
details:
What it does

  • Map of field outlines over Ukraine (Fields of The World) and the 48 contiguous US states (USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries); tap a field to open its card.
  • History strip: eleven seasons per field, each a satellite estimate with its confidence; "?" where clouds left too few clear looks. The farmer can correct any year.
  • "Sow next": crops grown nearby, each with a 0–100 season score (water, heat, soil, disease — not a yield forecast); the farmer chooses. "Avoid": rules such as Ukraine's minimum return intervals (Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 164), with the year a crop becomes allowed again.
  • Risks per crop as "x of N years" from NASA POWER; a watch calendar with dates for this field's cell.
  • Compare rotations: "As now", "Balanced", "Drought-proof" and an editable "My plan"; combos and anti-combos between seasons; a climate switch (all years / last 10 / dry years only); five explanation items per plan: why suggested, evidence, benefits, information gaps, check locally.
  • "Why?": eight evidence charts (greenness against the field's own range, bare-soil months, rain in the critical window, heat and frost, root-zone moisture, then and now, terrain, soil), each with its source and resolution.
  • Priorities and constraints: what matters most, missing machinery, crops the farmer cannot sell, irrigation; banned crops are never suggested and are shown greyed with the reason.
  • A private "unsafe" flag for fields the farmer cannot work (for example debris), stored only locally.

How it works

NASA HLS greenness per field and ten-day period → seasonal curves → a classifier (gradient boosting) assigns each field-season to winter crop, summer crop or fallow → a transparent rule engine (crop calendars derived from the cell's own temperatures, return intervals, predecessor effects, hazards) scores every candidate plan. The site is static (GitHub Pages); all scoring runs in the browser.

Validation, including what failed

  • Winter/summer/fallow: accuracy 95.3 % against the KPI / World Bank crop maps (2019–2024) on held-out tiles (24,626 field-seasons); fallow is the weak class (F1 0.22). Outside the training oblast: Dnipropetrovsk 95.0 %, Kharkiv 94.2 %, Volyn 88.6 %, Lviv 87.2 %, Odesa 79.3 %.
  • Crop names in Ukraine: two models trained on the 2020 crop type map of Ukraine (Zenodo 11065080) reach summer macro-F1 0.83 (maize 0.90, sunflower 0.77) and winter macro-F1 0.85 on held-out tiles, and the geography is right (sunflower leads in the south and east, maize in the west and north). But trained on one year, their yearly shares swing in the 2024 drought, so crop names are shown only as "maybe …" hints and the rules never use them. Two earlier models trained on US labels (Red River Valley, then 160 tiles across the USA; macro-F1 0.75 and 0.74 on held-out US tiles) gave implausible crop shares in Ukraine and were dropped.
  • USA: field history 2018–2025 is USDA CDL, not our model. The rule set for US crops has fewer sources: 91 of its 191 values have none yet and are shown as "not yet verified". The 2026 US season shows only winter / summer / not cultivated; it has not been checked against a US map.
  • POWER climate checked against published Cherkasy normals (docs/VALIDATION.md).

Who it is for and limits

Farmers and agronomists planning the next seasons; it supports, and does not replace, an agronomist. It cannot see soil nitrogen, weeds, pests or prices; weather is at about 50 km, soil at 250 m; history is an estimate and says so.

Tools

Python (pipeline), TypeScript, React, MapLibre GL, PMTiles, Vitest; GitHub Pages.

Use of SI

  • The product idea came from the team: a map where tapping a field opens a game-like card with what to sow, what not to sow, the risks and what to watch; rotations as combos; date-aware planning; sunflower overuse as the core local problem. Every product decision was the team's.
  • Suggested by SI in discussion and adopted by the team: reconstructing crop history from yearly greenness curves with a classifier, the timeline-lanes layout of the comparison, the climate-scenario switch and the "x of N years" risk wording, and the choice of datasets, stack and validation design (the full split is in docs/PLAN.md §3 in the repository).
  • An SI coding assistant (Claude, through Claude Code, Anthropic) was used for research on data sources, planning support, writing the pipeline and web code, and drafting English texts, which the team reviewed and edited. The plan document was written with it before the 09:00 start; code and data work began on 14 Nov.
  • The logo (the "LAN" wordmark with a wheat ear) is SI-assisted: it is based on an image generated with Google Gemini and redrawn as vector by our code. The app and the demo deck use only the plain text name "Lan".
  • The product contains three machine-learning models trained by us on open labels, each with its accuracy reported: the season-group classifier (winter / summer / not cultivated) and two crop-name classifiers (summer and winter crops) whose output is shown only as hints. Recommendations come from transparent rules, not from a language model.

Try it

Demo field with a one-minute guide: https://nazariipolishchuk.github.io/lan/?demo=1 · Code (MIT): https://github.com/nazariipolishchuk/lan
dataRefs: NASA HLS Vegetation Indices v2.0 (HLSL30_VI, HLSS30_VI): field greenness curves, crop history
projectRefs: Fields of The World, global field boundaries (CC-BY-4.0): Ukrainian field outlines
KPI winter/summer crop maps of Ukraine 2019-2024, World Bank DDH 0066913 (CC-BY-4.0): training and validation labels
10 m crop type map of Ukraine 2020, Chen, Tu et al. 2024 (CC-BY-4.0): labels for crop-name hints
USDA NASS Crop Sequence Boundaries 2018-2025 with CDL codes (public domain): US field outlines and crop history
ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 (CC-BY-4.0): soil texture, organic carbon, pH
geoBoundaries gbOpen UKR ADM1 (ODbL 1.0): oblast outlines
Resolution No. 164 of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (2010): crop return intervals
Full reference list: software, fonts, extension sources for rules, with licences
